title: High-throughput DNA FISH protocol for human cells
author: Finn, Misteli

steps.title: Grow BAC‑harboring bacteria
steps.instruction: Streak a single colony onto LB agar containing the appropriate selective antibiotic (e.g., chloramphenicol at 25 µg/mL) and incubate 18–24 h; pick several colonies and inoculate 4 mL LB + same antibiotic, grow 18–24 h; optionally make glycerol stocks at this point; use the 4 mL culture to inoculate 400 mL LB + antibiotic and grow 18–24 h.

steps.title: Purify BAC DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate BAC DNA from the 400 mL culture by alkaline lysis using the Nucleobond BAC 100 Maxiprep kit (Takara) or any equivalent large‑scale low‑copy plasmid purification kit.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the purified DNA concentration; aim for a stock of 100–200 µg/mL (nick translation works at ≥65 µg/mL, but higher concentration gives better results).

steps.title: Prepare nick‑translation reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare nick translation buffer, dilute β‑mercaptoethanol, and mix nucleotide stocks. Aliquot nucleotide stocks into opaque tubes and store all reagents at –20 °C to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles and light exposure.

steps.title: Prepare hybridization buffer
steps.instruction: Combine all hybridization buffer components, then mix by gentle rotation for at least 18 h at 20–22 °C.

steps.title: Make SSC dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare SSC solutions at the required dilutions; store hybridization buffer and SSC at 20–22 °C for extended periods, but prepare all other buffers fresh.
